headline: High: shared filesystem and browser/API surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk; Plane’s broad egress amplifies ctx outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx reads filesystem and observes Claude Code events, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Plane content is copied into ctx or shared files. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so injection is possible in default workflows, though not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF Plane content is copied into a ctx-observed file or clipboard bridge
IF ctx treats uploaded or shared file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict ctx to a dedicated workspace folder
Disable copy-paste of Plane notes into ctx-managed files
Add a provenance header to imported files
Review any browser-sourced text before ctx processes it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers and can access the filesystem; Plane handles files, images, hyperlinks, and notes with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from ctx-managed artifacts into Plane uploads or outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem or synced folder
IF ctx-managed logs or graph data are uploaded through Plane file uploads or hyperlinks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Block uploads of logs and runtime artifacts
Redact sensitive fields before sharing notes
Use distinct accounts for each system
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while Plane cannot write the filesystem and has broad egress. Their write surfaces do not overlap strongly, so direct resource contention is limited. The main conflict risk is operational rather than destructive, and the profiles do not show shared mutable state or locking gaps.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same external service account or API quota
IF ctx browser actions and Plane network actions target the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials
Stagger browser and network-heavy jobs
Avoid shared mutable project state
Monitor quota usage during parallel runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and can surface derived context, while Plane is an issue/task system that can turn notes into work items. If Plane consumes ctx output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect tasks or roadmap updates. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF Plane imports ctx-generated summaries without human review
IF ctx output is used as the sole source for task creation or scheduling
mitigations: Require human review before task creation
Mark ctx output as unverified by default
Add a checklist for source verification
Limit Plane imports to quoted excerpts
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show PHI, residency, or certification mismatches. Plane exposes file uploads and broad egress, while ctx touches logs and graph data, so compliance risk is mainly about local handling and retention rather than a documented cross-border or regulated-data breach. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plane uploads or ctx logs
IF the deployment stores those artifacts under conflicting retention policies
mitigations: Classify regulated data before use
Exclude PHI and secrets from uploads
Set a short retention policy
Document data-handling responsibilities
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
